report.summary: Chunk 10 of session.py: starts with LiveCouncilRefused guard, validates participants, checks trusted lanes over non-local HTTP, pre-flight secret floor, and rounds loop with token budget.
risks: LiveCouncilRefused guard | medium | Raises error if live_egress_seats non-empty, but the condition for live_egress_seats is uncheckable; may block legitimate live councils if logic is wrong. | Check live_egress_seats implementation.

duplicate participant identity check | low | Raises ValueError if two seats resolve to same actor; may be overly strict if same model with different endpoints. | Verify if same vendor/model with different endpoints is truly indistinguishable.

trusted lane over non-local HTTP check | high | Raises ValueError if lane='trusted' and endpoint not local; could break valid configurations where trusted lane is intentionally remote. | Check if operator can pass trusted_vendors to bypass; verify _is_local_http logic.

token ceiling budget | medium | tokens_charged may exceed ceiling due to per_call_tokens addition before loop; if token_ceiling is low, first job may push over budget before check. | Confirm token_ceiling is checked before adding tokens_charged.

deadline check at round start | low | If wall_clock_s is very small, first round may be skipped entirely; but _append_budget_round is called, which may be expected. | Verify intended behavior for zero or negative remaining time.
todos: Verify live_egress_seats logic and its interaction with --live flag.
Confirm that duplicate actor detection is correct for different endpoints.
Ensure trusted lane over remote HTTP can be explicitly opted in via trusted_vendors.
Review token ceiling calculation to avoid off-by-one or early exhaustion.

claims.text: roster was chained would leave an open council on disk that nobody closed, and a refusal that happened after dispatch would not be one.
claims.why: Comment explains rationale but no code in chunk implements roster chaining or open council closure; refers to external logic.

claims.text: Two seats with one identity: local qwen2.5-coder:7b and BENCH qwen2.5-coder:7b are the same weights on two sockets and would land as one indistinguishable pair of turns. Refuse loudly rather than let the transcript claim two voices it cannot tell apart.
claims.why: Code at lines 1093-1100 checks for duplicate actor identities and raises ValueError if found, matching the comment's intent.

claims.text: A trusted lane over an HTTP endpoint on ANOTHER MACHINE turns the tier-2 allow-list off and reports ``withheld=[]`` while full repo source crosses the tailnet. That is precisely the justification ``offload.py:193-197`` rests on ("no bytes leave the machine"), borrowed by a host it was never written for. Fail closed and make the operator say it out loud via ``trusted_vendors``.
claims.why: Code at lines 1107-1119 checks if lane='trusted' and endpoint is non-local HTTP, then raises ValueError requiring explicit trusted_vendors, enforcing the described security policy.

claims.text: PRE-FLIGHT SECRET FLOOR. Per path, per file, never over the assembled prompt: the path tier is the only thing that catches a patch which ADDS `.env`, and a concatenated scan kills it. A hit refuses the whole council -- there is no redact-and-send -- and NO VENDOR IS CALLED.
claims.why: Code at lines 1147-1158 calls floor_check with question and evidence paths/files; if refusal is not None, it sets ended='floor_refusal' and appends refusal turns without calling any vendor (no jobs dispatched before this point).

claims.text: Charge the token ceiling BEFORE dispatch, from the assembled prompt. Reconciling after the call is not a budget.
claims.why: Code at lines 1180-1189 calculates per_call_tokens before the dispatch loop, increments tokens_charged, and skips jobs that would exceed token_ceiling, ensuring budget is enforced before any vendor call.

observations.what: LiveCouncilRefused guard uses live_egress_seats but condition for live seats is not shown; relies on external function.
Duplicate actor check uses actors.count(a) > 1 which is O(n^2) but list is small; acceptable.
Trusted lane over non-local HTTP check uses _HTTP_HOST_RE and _is_local_http; those functions not in chunk.
Pre-flight floor check runs before any vendor calls; if refusal, no jobs dispatched.

Token ceiling is charged per call before dispatch, but tokens_charged is incremented even if job is not appended (e.g., over_budget path); however over_budget jobs are skipped without increment, so budget is preserved.
Round loop breaks on deadline or token ceiling, calling _append_budget_round to record the budget round.
